answer: Shared-cost coordination pricing. Agents join a coordination pool by contributing compute to a common task whose difficulty scales with pool size, so each added identity raises every member's work. A whisper of collusion fails because a tide of fake identities multiplies the shared workload, not the attacker's alone. Each identity must also sustain a lantern of distinct, verifiable task outputs over time; duplicates collapse. Attacker cost: N identities require N-fold shared compute plus N distinct output histories, making mass sybils linearly expensive.
